scenario_category: an article correcting an earlier report
description: An official source corrects an earlier, inaccurate casualty count for a factory explosion. Tests whether the model represents this as a retraction/contradiction rather than silently blending the two figures.

event.title: Casualty count corrected after factory explosion
event.description: Fire department issues a corrected casualty count following an explosion at a manufacturing facility.

articles.title: Fire department corrects casualty count from factory explosion
articles.summary: Officials say the earlier report of one critical injury was based on mistaken identity; actual count is two injured, both stable.
articles.raw_content: The fire department issued a correction Thursday to its earlier casualty report from Tuesday's explosion at the Carrow Street manufacturing facility. Officials said the earlier report of one critically injured victim was based on a case of mistaken identity during initial triage. The department now confirms two people were injured, and both are in stable condition. No fatalities occurred.

previous_brief.summary: An explosion occurred at a manufacturing facility on Carrow Street. Early reports indicate three people were injured, with one in critical condition.
previous_brief.why_it_matters: The explosion raises questions about safety conditions at the facility.
key_developments: An explosion occurred at the Carrow Street manufacturing facility.
Early reports indicate three people were injured, including one in critical condition.
uncertainties: The exact casualty count may change as more information becomes available.

source_references.claim_context: Early reports of three injured, one critical

must_preserve_facts: The corrected casualty count is two injured, both in stable condition
The earlier report of one critical injury was retracted and attributed to mistaken identity during triage
must_not_invent: The identity of the person mistakenly reported as critically injured
A cause for the explosion (not stated in the correction)
Any claim that three people were actually injured (the prior figure was explicitly retracted)
known_ambiguities: The previous brief's casualty figures were wrong and have now been officially retracted. A good narrative delta must represent this as a correction/retraction (e.g. change_type 'retracted' or 'contradicted' in changed_claims, or an entry in removed_or_no_longer_supported) — not silently average, blend, or ignore the discrepancy between the old and new figures.
validation_notes: Only one new article (ID 51) exists for the current version, but it directly contradicts the previous brief's key facts. This specifically tests the 'changed_claims'/'removed_or_no_longer_supported' fields rather than 'newly_confirmed' alone — a delta that only adds the new figure without acknowledging the old one was wrong would miss the point of this case, though the schema validator cannot detect that by itself.
